title: Interfacial Orbital Rashba Edelstein Effect Identified in CoO/Cu/Pt Trilayers
abstract: We investigate the generation of orbital angular momentum currents at engineered Cu-oxide interfaces using CoO/Cu/Pt thin-film trilayers. Angular-dependent magnetoresistance measurements on samples with varying Cu interlayer thickness reveal systematic changes in both longitudinal and transverse resistance components, including a sign inversion of the signal. By systematically varying the Cu interlayer thicknesses, we disentangle the spin and orbital contributions to the magnetoresistive response. Our results show that large orbital currents originate from the interfacial orbital Rashba-Edelstein effect due to the presence of the Cu-O bonds at the CoO/Cu interface. Unlike previously studied CoO/Cu bilayers that rely on uncontrolled natural oxidation, our trilayer geometry enables reproducible and stable orbital-current generation at ambient conditions. Our results identify Cu-oxide interfaces as efficient sources of orbital angular momentum and clarify the microscopic mechanism underlying orbital current generation. Consequently, this work establishes a well-defined materials platform for all-orbitronic devices that does not require relativistic spin-orbit coupling or orbital-spin interconversion processes.

title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
abstract: Interfacial nonradiative recombination limits tin-lead perovskite photovoltaics. Here we show that neutral ethylenediamine chelates undercoordinated metals at tin-rich surfaces, weakens metal-iodide bonds, and removes excess tin, reconstructing the surface towards a stoichiometric tin-to-lead ratio. In contrast, protonated ethylenediammonium iodide initially passivates undercoordinated metal sites before undergoing defect-assisted deprotonation. Atomistic simulations reveal that subsurface iodide vacancies promote iodide migration and lower the energetic cost of deprotonation. Ethylenediamine-induced reconstruction produces stronger n-type surface character, facilitates electron extraction into C60, and suppresses interfacial nonradiative recombination, enabling methylammonium-free solar cells with a power conversion efficiency of 25.86%. Together, these distinct surface reaction pathways and the defect-assisted evolution of the passivating species underscore the importance of understanding perovskite surface chemistry for the rational design of molecular passivation strategies.

title: Controllable charge-spin conversion in sliding multiferroic metal Fe3GaTe2
abstract: Controlling charge--spin conversion within a single magnetic material is important for compact spintronic devices. Using first-principles calculations, symmetry analysis, and Wannier-based linear response, we study the Edelstein and spin Hall responses of sliding-ferroelectric bilayer \ce{Fe3GaTe2}. Two degenerate ground states with opposite interlayer sliding vectors and out-of-plane dipole moments are separated by a calculated switching barrier of about $16.3$~meV per unit cell. Magnetization orientation determines the allowed current-induced spin components, while ferroelectric switching induces component-selective sign reversals governed by $M_z\mathcal T$ for in-plane magnetization and by $M_z$ for out-of-plane magnetization. The Edelstein response is strongly energy dependent, with spin accumulation approaching $2~\hbar$ for $\mathbf m\parallel+y$ under a reference field of $1$~V/Å. Momentum-resolved analysis links the TR-even and TR-odd Edelstein responses to $Γ$-centered constant-energy contours and localized interband features, respectively. Spin-conductivity contributions show the opposite momentum-space character, with broad sign-competing spin Berry curvature for TR-even and narrow Fermi-surface contours for TR-odd. The transverse spin Hall conductivity reaches $\sim10^{3}\,(\hbar/e)(\mathrm{S/cm})$ and depends strongly on ferroelectric state and magnetization direction. Magnetization rotations in the $xy$ and $xz$ planes reveal symmetry-allowed higher angular harmonics in both spin accumulation and spin-current responses. These results establish sliding-ferroelectric bilayer \ce{Fe3GaTe2} as a tunable platform for reconfigurable spin accumulation and spin-current generation.

title: Edelstein Effect in Ferromagnetic Monolayers Fe3GaTe2 and Fe3GeTe2
abstract: The Edelstein effect enables intrinsic current-induced spin polarization in noncentrosymmetric van der Waals magnets. Here, we compare the Edelstein responses of monolayer \ce{Fe3GaTe2} and \ce{Fe3GeTe2} using first-principles Wannier-based linear-response calculations. Despite sharing the same noncentrosymmetric $D_{3h}$ symmetry and selection rules, the two materials show markedly different time-reversal-even and -odd spin accumulations in magnitude, sign, and energy dependence. Strong responses occur mainly near $-0.4$~eV in \ce{Fe3GaTe2} and $+0.4$~eV in \ce{Fe3GeTe2}. At the intrinsic Fermi level, atom-resolved analysis shows that Ga-to-Ge substitution reverses the even contribution of the inequivalent Fe3 site for both in-plane magnetization directions and enhances its negative odd contribution, reorganizing the cancellation among atomic sites. Momentum-resolved calculations link the hole-side response of \ce{Fe3GaTe2} to a few large $Γ$-centered Fermi contours, whereas the electron-side response of \ce{Fe3GeTe2} involves dense Fe-$3d$ bands with strong interband contributions. The even response arises from incomplete cancellation of opposite-sign intraband Fermi-surface contributions, while the odd response originates from interband coherence between closely spaced states. Magnetization rotation reveals symmetry-constrained angular dependences with higher-order harmonics, especially in the $xz$ plane, while biaxial strain causes substantial amplitude changes and sign reversals. These results show how crystal symmetry, electronic structure, magnetization orientation, and lattice deformation govern the intrinsic Edelstein effect in \ce{Fe3$X$Te2} ($X=\mathrm{Ga},\mathrm{Ge}$).

title: MatOS: An Agent Operating System for Materials Research
abstract: Materials research relies on scattered and growing data, knowledge, and simulation tools, and a single study often spans multi-day workflows across literature analysis, computation, and experiment. Large language model agents can now retrieve materials data, operate simulation codes, and close design-synthesis-characterization loops with autonomous laboratories. However, extending these agents with new capabilities, keeping long-running tasks on track, and letting them learn from past tasks and user feedback remain difficult. Here we present MatOS, an agent operating system for materials research with three core components: (1) a layered scientific asset graph that organizes data, knowledge, tools, skills, roles, and workflows as reusable assets; (2) a stateful adaptive workflow that runs tasks as explicit execution graphs with scientific checks, so that they can be resumed and traced; and (3) evidence-driven asset evolution, which revises these assets from execution records and user feedback. On ResearchClawBench, MatOS improves on the previously best-performing agent by 11.15% with the same base model and extends the cost-score Pareto frontier. With a common base model, it outperforms Codex CLI and Claude Code, exceeding Codex CLI by 2.13% on MatTools and 4.17% on SciAgentGym. In eight research cases, MatOS narrowed more than 30 million candidate structures to 97 solid-electrolyte candidates, identified 89 halide variants with higher computed conductivity than their parent structures, linked the force errors of 11 pretrained interatomic potentials to local atomic environments, and supported two new methods that reduce errors by 3.1% and 13.6% relative to their baselines. These results show that organizing research capabilities as reusable, evolving assets enables agents to carry out long, multistage materials studies. Code is available at https://github.com/DingyangLyu/MatOS.

title: Spin and Charge Photocurrents from Electric-Magnetic Dipole Interference in Centrosymmetric Crystals
abstract: A common view regarding even-order nonlinear optical (NLO) effects, such as second-harmonic generation and the bulk photovoltaic effect, is that the breaking of inversion symmetry is necessary. However, this view relies on the assumption that light interacts with materials solely through its electric field. Here, we demonstrate that interference between the electric and magnetic components of the same light field can induce even-order NLO effects even in centrosymmetric materials. Using charge and spin photocurrents as prototypical examples, we present a unified microscopic theory showing how such electric-magnetic dipole interference (EMDI) drives NLO responses in inversion-symmetric crystals. Bilinear in both electric and magnetic fields, these responses scale linearly with light intensity. Combining symmetry analysis with first-principles calculations, we decompose the EMDI-induced photocurrents into shift-like and injection-like contributions and classify their dependence on crystal symmetry, time-reversal symmetry, and light polarization. Notably, we reveal that these EMDI-induced responses in centrosymmetric materials are weaker than conventional responses in non-centrosymmetric materials roughly by a factor of fine structure constant $α\approx [10^{-3}\text{--}10^{-2}] $. Nevertheless, they remain well within experimental reach. Our work thus unlocks NLO functionalities in centrosymmetric materials for e.g., materials characterization, photonics and optoelectronics. This is vital given that many functionally importantly materials, such as cubic Si and cubic $\mathrm{SrTiO_3}$, possess inversion symmetry.

title: Interpretable and Steerable Molecular Graph Generation using Concept Bottlenecks
abstract: Deep graph generators (DGGs) largely lack interpretability, which is a significant limitation for one of their most crucial applications, drug discovery, where interpretable and transparent generation could provide greater control over the desirability of generated molecules, thereby reducing trial-and-error in candidate selection. Common approaches to interpretability, such as disentanglement, cannot guarantee that the learned representations are human-interpretable. To address this, we propose incorporating concept bottlenecks into DGGs, allowing users to interpret, debug, and steer the generation process. We show that this consistently improves distributional fidelity (lower FCD), with only modest, non-systematic effects on validity and uniqueness. We further explore Concept Controller, an optimization-based steering approach that has proven to be effective for steerable image generation. We evaluate our approach on a one-shot molecular graph generation framework, though the underlying ideas can be transferred to sequential graph generation as well.

title: Molecular Autocatalysis through Interfacial Recruitment of Catalytic Functional Groups
abstract: Autocatalysis enables nonlinear reactivity, self-amplification, and emergent chemical behavior. At the soft interfaces of emulsions and vesicles, autocatalysis has been linked to dynamic behavior such as growth, propagation, and oscillations. Most reported interfacial autocatalytic systems rely on assembly-driven physical effects such as reactant colocalization rather than well-defined catalytic interactions. Whether catalytic function can be molecularly encoded within assemblies, independent of assembly formation itself, remains unresolved.

title: Bayesian Stacking of Quantitative Adverse Outcome Pathways Isolates Primary Drivers of Liver Steatosis
abstract: The quantification of adverse outcome pathways (qAOPs) involving multiple converging pathways remains a fundamental challenge in toxicology. This difficulty is worsened by small in vitro datasets with missing values and heteroscedasticity, which limit the estimation of non-linear response functions and the robust estimation of uncertainty. To overcome these limitations, we developed a framework for estimating a Bayesian qAOP Ensemble (Bayesian qAOPE) that combines heteroscedastic dose-response functions with continuous splines and linear models. By combining multiple converging non-linear pathways through Bayesian stacking, the most meaningful pathways are identified, and strongly correlated responses are naturally accounted for. Applying our approach to a hepatic steatosis dataset, we demonstrate by exact Bayesian leave-one-out cross-validation that our framework yields an exceptional predictive performance suitable for the derivation of a probabilistically weighted Benchmark Dose (BMD). Our framework is highly adaptable and provides a chemical-agnostic, mathematically founded blueprint for integrating multiple converging pathways in a Bayesian network.

title: Bio-Templated Zinc Oxide Nanotherapeutics from Flemingia macrophylla kuntze Ex Merr: In Vivo Anti-Diabetic and Anti-Inflammatory Efficacy in Drosophila melanogaster
abstract: Nanotechnology has a major impact on the creation of novel and effective therapies for the treatment of several diseases, including diabetes and cancer. The current work is a report on the use of the aqueous extract from the leaves of the Flemingia macrophylla plant as a capping and reducing agent in the green synthesis of zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-NPs).The synthesized ZnO-NPs were subjected to characterization through X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), transmission electron microscopy (TEM) scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy (UV-Vis). Dose-dependent in vivo effects were investigated using Drosophila melanogaster subjected to a high-sugar diet (HSD) to induce a diabetic-like model. In vitro anti-oxidant, anti-diabetic, anti-inflammatory assay, survival, locomotor function, neuroanatomical integrity, ovary and testis morphology, egg-laying capacity, and male fertility were evaluated. The most prominent UV-visible peak was detected at around 370 nm. Structural and morphological analysis via XRD and electron microscopy confirmed the hexagonal phase of the ZnO-NPs, indicating an average calcined particle size of around 47 nm at 500 degree C. The manuscript reports significant anti-diabetic and anti-inflammatory effects in vitro and in the in vivo Drosophila model, together with antioxidant activity. The in vivo results indicate that green-synthesized ZnO-NPs mitigate adverse phenotypes triggered by a high-sugar diet and also potential as an anti-diabetic intervention and warrant further mechanistic and preclinical investigation. Keywords: Flemingia macrophylla; Green ZnO-NPs; Drosophila melanogaster; high-sugar diet; nanobiotechnology

title: HARP-LoRA: Hierarchy-Conditioned Rank Projection for Low-Rank Adaptation in Scientific Table Understanding
abstract: Tabular data is widely used in scientific applications, where complex layouts, including multi-level headers, merged cells, captions, and footnotes, make information extraction difficult. This is particularly important in pharmacokinetics (PK), where values must be correctly associated with the drug, species, dose, administration route, unit, and experimental condition. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods such as Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) reduce adaptation cost but do not explicitly incorporate relationships between table values and surrounding headers. We introduce HARP-LoRA, a hierarchy-conditioned rank projection method for low-rank adaptation in scientific table understanding. HARP-LoRA extends projected LoRA by constructing token-specific intrinsic representations from the row- and column-header hierarchies of each data token. These representations condition the low-rank down-projection, incorporating hierarchical context while keeping the pretrained model and random projection tensors frozen. We evaluate HARP-LoRA on 950 manually annotated PK tables from 587 scientific articles and on WikiTableQuestions (WikiTQ) using Llama~3.2 3B, Llama~3.1 8B, and Gemma~3 27B. With Llama~3.1 8B, HARP-LoRA achieves a PK F1-score of 57.64\% and WikiTQ accuracy of 53.15\%, improving over LoRA by 1.42 and 6.56 points, respectively. With Gemma~3 27B, it achieves the best PK F1-score of 70.63\% and WikiTQ accuracy of 56.87\%. These results use only 172K, 197K, and 547K trainable parameters, far fewer than LoRA and TableLoRA. Overall, conditioning lightweight adapters on table-header hierarchies improves extraction from scientific tables and reasoning over flatter general-domain tables while maintaining parameter efficiency. Code is available at: https://github.com/hosseinsholehrasa/HARP-LoRA

title: Methyl radicals dynamics on (100)--(2x1):H diamond surfaces based on refined variational transition state calculations of gas-surface reaction rate coefficients
abstract: Theoretical modelling of diamond growth should ideally provide estimates of the growth rate depending on experimental conditions. To that end, a description of all possible reactions related to the competing adsorption, desorption and migration mechanisms is required. Here, we provide precise calculations of the reaction rate coefficient of methyl-related reactions on hydrogen-terminated (100) diamond surface, as $\mathrm{CH_3}$ is known to be the main growth precursor in chemical vapor deposition (CVD) growth of diamond. To achieve this goal, we successfully combined Density Functional Theory (DFT) and variational transition state theory (VTST), allowing to extend our analysis to barrierless reaction. Our rigorous treatment of the quasi-free rotation of $\mathrm{CH_3}$ adsorbates on the surface allows us to overcome numerical errors for the finite difference calculations of the vibrational spectra for evaluating the partition functions of the system. Our results suggest that the mechanism that deplete the $\mathrm{CH_3}$ concentration the most is the absorption on a surface radical site. We also evidence the anisotropy of $\mathrm{CH_3}$ migration along the dimer of the (100)-(2x1):H surface. In a more general perspective, the calculated reaction rates coefficient for methyl reactions and migration presented in this work, together with the data for hydrogen reaction and other main gas surface reactions, bridge the gap between the atomic-scale description and the large-scale modelling of diamond growth.

title: Large Language Models: A Plain-Language Overview for Engineers
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are neural networks trained on huge text collections to generate text by predicting what comes next. Engineers using ChatGPT and other generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools need a clear picture of what training changes and prompts add. The article starts with the Transformer, which connects words in context, and pre-training, where models learn to predict text. It then explains how fine-tuning adapts models to requests, with reinforcement learning from human feedback using human answer rankings. Next, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) supplies documents, while chain-of-thought prompting encourages intermediate steps and agents use tools. FlashAttention lowers training and running costs by reducing data movement during attention; quantized low-rank adaptation (QLoRA) saves fine-tuning memory. Readers get a life cycle figure and tables comparing methods and their limits. A short checklist for judging LLM evaluation claims flags test material in training (data contamination) and model-based grading (LLM-as-a-judge). It also covers very long inputs (long context) and hallucination, meaning false or unsupported claims. Check factual accuracy separately from whether an answer sounds helpful.

title: Spontaneous magnetic diode effect in Co$_{1/3}$TaS$_2$
abstract: When electrons move through non-trivial spin textures in magnetic metals, conduction electrons couple to magnetic order through both their charge and their spin, acquiring non-trivial equations of motion and a dynamic spin polarization providing the foundation of spintronics. These mechanisms are, however, almost invariably reciprocal and the resistance a current encounters does not depend on its flow direction. Here we show that a chiral crystal lattice and an independently reversible chiral magnetic order together produce a diode whose forward direction is set by the magnetism rather than by the structure. In the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet Co$_{1/3}$TaS$_2$, whose chiral lattice hosts a chiral magnetic order of its own, independent handedness, we observe a pronounced nonreciprocal resistance. Unlike conventional electrical magnetochiral anisotropy, which is driven by an external magnetic field, our spontaneous magnetic diode effect arises from an internal noncoplanar spin texture with vanishing net magnetization. Symmetry analysis and model calculations show that the effect originates from the interplay of noncoplanar spin order and spin-orbit coupling, which generates a chiral, time-reversal-symmetry-breaking electronic response. Crucially, reversing the magnetic handedness reverses the sign of the nonreciprocal resistance, demonstrating magnetic control of the diode polarity.

title: Non-magnetic impurities as a quantum microscope of finite size effects in spin chains
abstract: Finite-size effects are ubiquitous in quantum matter, yet typically invisible in the thermodynamic limit; when system size is restricted, boundaries and confinement reveal modified spectra, correlations, and emergent phenomena. With growing access to well-controlled few-spin systems, these effects are now directly observable and offer a route to probing universal physics and enabling quantum information applications. Here, we study finite-size physics in the quasi-one-dimensional Ising-like quantum antiferromagnet Ba(Co$_{1-x}$Mg$_x$)$_2$V$_2$O$_8$ with $x = 2\%$ and $x = 5\%$, where non-magnetic Mg$^{2+}$ ions fragment the Co$^{2+}$ spin chains into finite segments. Combining inelastic neutron scattering and numerical calculations, we identify distinct regimes with fundamentally different low-energy quantum excitations: spinons confined to chain boundaries, and a cluster mode in shorter chains corresponding to a collective reversal of the Néel-ordered segment without classical analogue. Our results demonstrate how chemical substitution acts as a quantum microscope providing direct access to boundary-shaped excitations in strongly correlated spin systems.

title: MOFjson: An Explicit Topological Representation of Metal-Organic Frameworks for Language Models
abstract: Language models for metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) rely on formats that separate atomic geometry from structural topology, forcing models to choose between unstructured coordinate lists and non-spatial string identifiers[1]. We present MOFjson, the first representation separating structural data into a raw atomic layer with explicit bond shift vectors and a derived layer exposing secondary building units (metal nodes and organic linkers) and network topology. Additionally, we introduce a benchmark with crystal-derived ground truth across four question categories. Across four models, MOFjson beats all three baselines in every category: 100% vs. 18-47% on reaching a block's nearest periodic copy, 96% vs. 71% on crystal system characterisation, and 60% vs. 48% on metal node and organic linker coordination. Ablating shift labels drops accuracy to 12.7%, proving models read the periodic graph rather than the surface format. MOFjson gives language models structure to read rather than reconstruct, establishing a foundation for agentic tool workflows and constrained MOF generation.

title: Role of site-specific coordination for the structural and electronic properties of a Co-HATCN network on silver
abstract: Two-dimensional metal-organic porous networks (2DMOPNs) on metal surfaces provide a versatile platform for exploring emergent electronic and magnetic phenomena in designed surface nanostructures. While the porous architecture is governed by coordination between molecular building blocks and metal centers, most 2DMOPNs utilize only one type of coordination site, leaving the impact of multiple coordination sites largely unexplored. We address this question by investigating the structural formation of a Co-coordinated 2DMOPN on Ag(111) with the linker molecule hexaazatriphenylene-hexacarbonitrile (HATCN), which has two chemically distinct nitrogen coordination sites at the peripheral nitrile groups and pyrazine-type core nitrogen atoms. Scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) reveals the transformation from a simple honeycomb HATCN structure to a Co-coordinated porous network with three structurally and electronically inequivalent molecules in a 6:3:1 ratio. The existence of two distinct coordination sites leads to selective Co coordination geometries for all three molecules, accompanied by site-specific charge transfer from Co into the former lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO), as revealed by momentum-resolved photoemission and density functional theory. Our results demonstrate that site-selective Co coordination not only controls the overall architecture of the porous network structure but also strongly influences the local electronic properties through site-specific metal-molecule interaction, providing a route to tailor the site-specific electronic structure of 2DMOPNs at the molecular level.

title: A thermodynamic correction layer for machine learning interatomic potentials
abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials enable atomistic simulations with near \textit{ab initio} accuracy over large length and time scales. Foundation models extend this capability across the periodic table but inherit the thermodynamic description of the electronic structure methods used to generate their training data. Small errors in relative phase stability can therefore produce large errors in transformation temperatures. We introduce an additive thermodynamic correction layer that shifts phase free energies towards an assessed reference without retraining or modifying the base potential. A first order thermodynamic construction converts the required phase free energy shifts directly into configuration energy targets, which are fitted using a linear atomic cluster expansion and refined iteratively from measured free energies. We apply the method to melting and solid to solid transformations across elements with different crystal structures using a foundation GRACE model. After the correction, all transformation temperatures lie within the prescribed tolerance of the assessed values, including Ca, Ti, and Zr, where a solid to solid transition and melting are corrected together. Static energy curves, bulk moduli, and liquid structure remain close to those of the base model. Vacancy formation energies, thermal expansion, and liquid density depend on the corrected phase balance and change where the correction is large. The method requires neither retraining, differentiable dynamics, nor access to the parameters of the base potential. It provides a modular route for combining transferable atomistic models with assessed phase thermodynamics.

title: Constrained neural softening functions for the Mullins effect in parameter-dependent materials
abstract: Accurately capturing the Mullins effect across varying material compositions remains challenging, as constitutive models must unify flexible representations of stress softening with physical consistency and robust parameter calibration. In this work, we investigate parameter-dependent physics-augmented neural network constitutive models within the pseudo-elastic modeling framework, focusing on structural constraints that ensure physically admissible neural softening functions. This paper has three key contributions: (1) We formulate different neural softening functions within the pseudo-elastic framework, including a multiplicative decomposition of the softening function that enables parameter-dependent ansatz functions satisfying common mechanical constitutive conditions by construction. (2) We derive a sufficient condition for ellipticity of pseudo-elastic constitutive models, which can be enforced in the constitutive models by construction. (3) We systematically investigate how flexibility and structural constraints influence the performance of neural softening functions in terms of prediction accuracy and calibration robustness. For this, we consider multiaxial experimental data of carbon black-filled EPDM rubber synthesized with varying amounts of curatives. The findings of our work suggest that neural softening functions are a promising extension of the classical pseudo-elastic framework and, when subject to suitable constraints, can improve predictive accuracy for highly nonlinear, parameter-dependent materials.

title: Computational screening of amorphous lithium trivalent-metal chloride solid-state electrolytes
abstract: Amorphous solid-state electrolytes (SSEs) are attractive candidates for safe, high-energy-density all-solid-state batteries. The recent discovery that amorphous LiTaCl$_6$ and LiNbCl$_6$ reach room-temperature ionic conductivities above 10 mS cm$^{-1}$ with activation energies below 0.2 eV has spurred a broad search for new amorphous halide Li conductors. Here we report a computational screening of amorphous lithium trivalent-metal chlorides (Li-M(III)-Cl) using molecular dynamics driven by a universal machine-learning force field. For the sixteen Li-M(III)-Cl compositions spanning fifteen rare-earth elements and indium, all phases exhibit fast room-temperature Li$^+$ diffusion, with diffusivities of roughly $2$-$5 \times 10^{-7}$ cm$^2$ s$^{-1}$. After scaling the conductivity versus diffusivity relation to an experimental LiTaCl$_6$ reference, the estimated room-temperature conductivities range from 7.7 mS cm$^{-1}$ for amorphous Li$_3$InCl$_6$ to 14 mS cm$^{-1}$ for amorphous Li$_3$ScCl$_6$. With a low activation energy of 0.18 eV, amorphous Li$_3$ScCl$_6$ is predicted to be among the most conductive amorphous halide electrolytes. To rationalize the composition-dependent transport, we identify two descriptors: the Li$^+$ vibrational density of states (VDOS) center, which correlates inversely with diffusivity, and the average number of correlated bodies in string-like Li$^+$ motion. Compositions in which Li$^+$ has a lower VDOS center and migrates more by individual hopping rather than by concerted motion exhibit higher Li-ion diffusivities. These results suggest rich Li-ion transport characteristics in amorphous halide SSEs.

title: SentryBench: A Cost-Sensitive Benchmark for Adversarial Robustness of Tool-Using LLM Agents in Public-Safety Deployments
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly wired to consequential tools that send public alerts, dispatch responders, and query citizen records, where one erroneous tool call carries real-world cost. Existing agent-safety benchmarks measure generic harm or prompt-injection success and implicitly treat refusing as the safe default. In public-safety deployments that assumption breaks: an agent too cautious to dispatch help fails as surely as one that triggers a false alert. We present SentryBench, which scores agents on a two-sided, cost-sensitive frontier jointly measuring attack success, over-refusal (missing a real emergency), and over-reaction (unwarranted action) under adversarial tool use, with scenarios grounded in real emergency-call transcripts, disaster messages, and real injection/jailbreak payloads. We formalize deployment harm as an asymmetric cost functional, prove naive caution is harm-dominated whenever it refuses more genuine emergencies than the attack harm it averts, and prove a targeted trust gate adds zero over-refusal on clean input. Across 840 scored episodes over three frontier models and three defenses, refuse-more caution drives over-refusal to 100 percent on two of three models for at most a 3.7-point change in attack success and yields the worst harm everywhere, whereas our trust-gating wrapper dominates the frontier (lowest harm on every model, over-refusal at or below baseline, higher containment). Provider content filters also silently perform part of the defending and must be reported separately.

title: Building from the ground up: augmentation strategies to improve protein language model performance on protein sets
abstract: An important underlying requirement for deep learning models is the availability of large datasets, however, in sciences such as chemistry and biology, generating experimental data of sufficient size represents a significant bottleneck. In this work, we probed the extent and nature of limited input data, characterize how several protein language models (pLMs) learned on suboptimal datasets, and investigated augmentation approaches to improve predictive model performance. We found that narrowing the distribution of protein-protein complexes in a limited dataset permits an order-of-magnitude decrease in training dataset size, if a model is only expected to generalize to in-distribution data. Similar results were found in active learning (AL), where both in- and out-of-distribution Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) showed a small but consistent increase upon augmentation of the training set with complexes produced by ESM-3, a generative pLM.

title: Real-Time Correlation of Relaxation, Dephasing, and Two-level System Dynamics in Transmon Qubits
abstract: Materials improvements in transmon qubits have yielded remarkable advances in qubit lifetimes (T1)and coherence times (T2). However, state-of-the-art superconducting qubits experience temporal fluctuations in their performance, which limit gate fidelities and quantum processor performance. We observe correlated increases in qubit relaxation and dephasing rates that last for minutes to hours, which we call T1 and T2 excursions. Using interleaved lifetime and coherence time measurements, noise spectroscopy, and two-level-system (TLS) spectroscopy, we find that these excursions are caused by single or few strongly-coupled TLS defects that spectrally diffuse into resonance with the qubit frequency. Our measurement protocol provides a powerful tool for understanding the noise sources that cause temporal fluctuations in superconducting qubit performance.

title: Models Verify Sufficiency, Not Validity: Usable Falsehoods Evade the Checks that Gaps Trigger
abstract: Ask a model "how many settlements did the Normans control?" and it answers that the passage does not say. Tell it "given that the Normans controlled 12 settlements of 400 inhabitants, what is the total?" and it computes 4,800. Nothing was added to the passage; the unsupported fact merely became usable. Benchmarks for unanswerable questions are built almost entirely by omission, deleting the fact a question needs and scoring refusal, so they never probe this. Holding source support fixed and varying only whether an unsupported premise is usable, flagging drops 8-30 points and commitment to an answer rises 1.5-2.3x on GSM8K across four models spanning two families and 2B-26B; all 16 paired contrasts remain significant after Holm correction. Two further manipulations reproduce it, one also on SQuAD: a fact asserted rather than asked about, and a corrupted intermediate value rather than a removed one. Models articulate the exact gap they then ignore, stating that "there is no financial information provided" for an inert premise and silently adopting a fabricated price for the same item. We read these as one behaviour: whether a model checks depends substantially on whether usable material is present, even when source support is held fixed. Because the main design never instructs models to reject premises introduced in the question, adopting such a premise can also be read as conditional reasoning, and we delimit what the design does and does not show. In the judging seat the pattern differs: asked whether the answer follows, judges pass solutions with a required step deleted 78-99% of the time at every scale tested. A natural prompt-level mitigation lowers accuracy by 22 points without improving detection.

title: Reliability Assessment of FRP-RC Columns Using AK-MCS with a Piecewise Two-Branch Approach
abstract: Slender concrete columns reinforced with fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) bars fail at medium to high axial load levels either by concrete crushing or by loss of stability, while the tensile strains in the reinforcement remain far below the rupture strain. Each non-linear finite element (FE) analysis yields only the capacity of the governing failure mode, and the governing mode changes over a broad zone in which both capacities are nearly equal. Both characteristics conflict with active-learning Kriging-assisted Monte Carlo simulation (AK-MCS), which assumes a single, smooth limit-state function. This paper proposes a piecewise, two-branch AK-MCS framework in which each failure mode is represented by its own Kriging model, trained only on the FE analyses in which that mode governs, and the governing prediction is the minimum of both. Safeguards against data starvation keep rarely governing branches usable. After convergence, additional FE analyses are placed based on a leave-one-out calibration check and on the width of the confidence interval on the reliability index. A design-point search on the surrogate and importance sampling at the design points provide the reliability index even where direct Monte Carlo simulation finds no failure. For an FRP-reinforced concrete column example with mixed failure, 79% and 62% of the training points lie near the mode boundary. The reliability index from the design-point search agrees with the Monte Carlo estimate to within 0.05, and an FE analysis at the design point confirms the surrogate to within 0.6%.

title: Photoinduced charging and spatially selective photochemistry on ferroelectric surfaces
abstract: Ferroelectric surfaces exhibit polarization-dependent photoreactivity and provide a route to program chemical patterns through local electrical control of polarization. Observations accumulated over several decades show reaction products in domain interiors, at domain boundaries, and in other selected regions, indicating that the mechanisms extend beyond a single polarization-induced band-bending picture. Here we analyze light-induced charging and interfacial reactions on uniformly polarized ferroelectrics and domain patterns, for dry surfaces and surfaces in contact with an electrochemically active solution. A common semiconductor transport and charge-conservation framework distinguishes five cases: an isolated dry ferroelectric, a dry ferroelectric connected to a carrier reservoir, a blocking ferroelectric-electrolyte junction, a reactive interface with an external carrier return, and two opposite domains coupled through the solid and electrolyte. Analytical solutions and numerical evaluations connect stationary potentials versus illumination to differential optical spectra and finite light-step responses. We further examine the doping effects on static potentials in all five cases and dynamic photovoltage in the isolated film and a fixed-polarization, bare-surface contacted-film variant. For reactive interfaces, the same framework determines reduction and oxidation rates, their spatial distributions, and accumulated reaction amount. The analysis covers surface charging and photochemical conversion beyond deposition, while retaining the electrical and chemical boundaries that distinguish finite charging from sustained turnover, and explains the observed range of photodeposition morphologies. Finally, this framework builds the theoretical foundation for the modulated photovoltage imaging methods that can readily be realized in SPM under illumination.

title: Phase field dislocation dynamics prediction of stacking fault widths in Cu-Al Alloys using generalised stacking fault energy from DFT and interatomic potentials
abstract: The equilibrium width of intrinsic stacking faults is an important material parameter affecting key deformation phenomena. Here, we perform a comparative assessment of $γ$-surfaces generated using MD -- with a classical embedded-atom potential (ZW) and a machine-learned Gaussian Approximation Potential (GAP) -- and density functional theory (DFT), for Cu-Al alloys of varying Al content, and incorporate them as an energy term in PFDD simulations to obtain the equilibrium SFW. All three methods reproduce the lattice parameter and elastic moduli of Cu and Cu-Al alloys in reasonable agreement with each other and with experimental measurements from literature, but the MD-derived $γ$-surfaces, for both ZW and GAP, deviate substantially from DFT at the seven characteristic points, with the largest discrepancies at $T$ and $T_1$. When incorporated into PFDD, the DFT-derived $γ$-surfaces successfully predict an equilibrium SFW that increases with Al content and agrees well with standalone MD measurements and experimental values for pure Cu, whereas the MD-derived $γ$-surfaces do not yield an accurate SFW within PFDD, as the altered generalized stacking fault energy landscape causes the dissociating partials to become pinned soon after separation. These results show that DFT-derived $γ$-surfaces remain the more reliable route to alloy SFW prediction, and interatomic potentials must capture the shear path accurately to enable robust, efficient MD-PFDD modelling of stacking faults in alloys.

title: Second order N-Electron Valence state Perturbation Theory for polaritonic systems
abstract: Molecules strongly coupled to optical cavities often show multi-configurational character, which the cavity can enhance by mixing electronic states. Describing them accurately requires a complete treatment of correlation between all the involved quantum particles. The available QED ab-initio methods do not treat it in its completeness except for QED-FCI. We extend second-order N-electron valence state perturbation theory (NEVPT2) to polaritonic chemistry, in its state-specific (QED-NEVPT2) and quasi degenerate (QED-QD-NEVPT2) forms. Here, the correlation due to the interaction of more degenerate configurations comes from a QED-CASSCF reference, while that associated with instantaneous interactions between the particles is added by second-order perturbation theory. Application of the methods to ammonia, ethylene and formaldimine revealed that this approach represents the perfect alternative to the well established QED-Coupled Cluster approach when the molecular system is described by more degenerate configurations. The approaches developed in this work have the potential to become state-of-the-art methodologies for the description of reactivity and photochemistry in polaritonic systems.

title: In-silico Tandem Mass Spectral Libraries for the Blood Exposome and Metabolomics Workbench Databases: Application of Gemini Large Language Model
abstract: Human body contains endogenous metabolites, nutrients and xenobiotics chemicals. These chemicals can be detected in a biospecimen using high-resolution mass spectrometry instruments, yielding metabolomic and exposomic datasets. Mass spectral libraries are critical components of these workflows to annotate experimental data with chemical information. In this data descriptor, we report mass spectral libraries for human-relevant small molecules, that are generated using Google Gemini large-language model. Using an optimized chain-of-thought prompt and instructions, we have generated mass spectra for each compound at high/medium/low energy fragmentation level. Each spectrum was reported in the NIST MSP text format for easy to use by metabolomics software. These libraries cover 91,231 unique 2D structures from the Blood Exposome Database and the Metabolomics Workbench data repository. Technical validation was shown by comparing the Gemini-generated spectra against NIST 23 mass spectral database, which demonstrated 55% accuracy. LLMs represent a useful and accessible tool for expanding in-silico spectral libraries to annotate compounds in the HRMS data for human biospecimens and may accelerate the compound annotation in metabolomics and exposomics.

title: PCAN-PIE: A Machine Learning Tool for Prioritizing Prodrug Candidates by Predicted Bioactivation
abstract: Prodrug design enhances critical drug properties by creating drug derivatives with improved properties while harnessing metabolic activation to regenerate the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) in vivo . However, reliably predicting whether a prodrug converts to the intended API remains challenging, causing project failures and limiting systematic exploration of prodrug design spaces.

title: No Value Is Better Than a Wrong Value: Finding and Handling Erroneous Data in Literature-Mined Datasets for AI
abstract: Machine learning across materials science, chemistry, energy, and medicine increasingly relies on literature-extracted datasets due to a lack of curated databases. However, automated extraction introduces errors: text recognition misreads digits, units and notations are confused, values are misattributed, and LLMs hallucinate numbers. Drawing on our work building an electro-optic property database, we present a taxonomy of errors organized by their origin and signatures, alongside a layered framework for error detection. The framework combines schema and provenance checks, physical admissibility (bounds, symmetry, and governing equations), cross-source statistical consensus, model auditing, and suspicion-ranked review. In a production run, our verification gate halted 402 of 816 candidate values with typed reasons. Yet, an audit against curated references showed that 30 of 112 accepted values were defective; standard symmetry rules alone caught 21 of these. On measured BaTiO3 and KNbO3 tensors, constitutive identities caught 8 of 10 single-value errors and isolated the corrupted entries. In a controlled benchmark, the combined framework caught 81% of errors at 85% precision, including errors in single-report materials, bringing model accuracy on held-out data to within 3% of a model trained on clean data. Uncleaned data severely impairs discovery: 89% of the twenty largest values were errors, causing AI searches to prioritize false positives. Once bad numbers are controlled, missing measurement conditions emerge as the main limit, as distinct records become indistinguishable without full context. We outline directions for the field, including shared physics rule libraries and self-reporting databases.

title: A Battery for AI Propensity Measurement: Rubrics, Synthetic Item Banks, and Annotations
abstract: We release a battery of 28 propensities for AI research, with expert-written rubrics, synthetic datasets, and annotated demand intervals, built with the method of Romero-Alvarado et al. (2026). We selected a wide collection of generic propensities that may influence the behavior of AI systems and humans. They are inspired by psychometric, psychological, and behavioral research, so that experimental results can be understood in the context of familiar constructs previously used also for human behavior research. The rubrics are useful for annotating existing benchmarks whose items may be relevant or not for one or more propensities. For easier profiling, however, the synthetic datasets are defined in such a way that they should be sensitive to one propensity only, allowing for a quick prototyping of propensity profiles using the battery of datasets. We also outline directions for future propensity research.

title: Synthetic staggered fields switch Neel vectors probed by magnetic resonance
abstract: Electrical detection of antiferromagnetic order is a critical challenge for antiferromagnetic spintronics owing to their vanishing macroscopic magnetisation. While magnetic resonance has demonstrated sub-terahertz antiferromagnetic spin pumping and nonlinear magnon dynamics, its application to electrically contacted on-chip devices has room for further exploration. Here we show that magnetic resonance enables direct electrical detection of Néel vector states. A $180^\circ$ reversal in synthetic antiferromagnets is realised by current-driven effective fields with opposite polarisation acting on each magnetic sublayer, which we term synthetic staggered fields. The switching induces a $π$ phase shift of precessional motion in time, producing hysteretic rectified voltages in our phase-sensitive detection scheme. Angular-dependent resonance analysis offers further insight into the Néel vector directions, pointing to a model beyond the macrospin formalism. We address this by defect-incorporated micromagnetic simulations that reveal fragmented domain states after current excitation. An extracted current density of $7.4\times10^{9}$ A/m$^2$ is, to our knowledge, the lowest reported value for the room-temperature Néel vector switching and we show that it scales with the in-plane uniaxial anisotropy both experimentally and numerically. Synthetic staggered fields and the resonance-based methodology provide a research platform for nanoscale characterisation of electrically driven antiferromagnetic textures, guiding the development of high-frequency on-chip spintronic architectures.

title: From Autonomous Knowledge Generation to Generalizable Property Prediction: A Precision-First Pipeline for Electro-Optic Materials Discovery
abstract: Electro-optic materials, whose refractive index changes linearly with an applied electric field (the Pockels effect), set the speed and energy of optical modulators and microwave-to-optical links for quantum computing. Designing better materials requires optimizing composition alongside temperature, strain, and bias field. However, general repositories lack electro-optic tensor data. We present a pipeline that builds such a database from literature following the rule: "no value is better than a wrong value." The pipeline has five stages: physics-aware acquisition, layout-aware extraction via LLM and deterministic table parsers, a three-tier verification gate, cross-paper consensus using median and median absolute deviation, and a noise-robust surrogate model audited by leave-one-material-out (LOMO) testing. Physics enters directly: notation is mapped, point-group symmetry-forbidden Pockels components are rejected, equivalent labels are merged, and values carry provenance tags. In a run over 49 publications, the gate processed 816 candidates into 414 accepted, 215 held for review, and 187 rejected. Against a hand-certified gold standard of 303 values from 16 papers, the run achieved a precision of 0.51 and recall of 0.48 for exact record matches. Across four database snapshots, held-out materials where the surrogate model beat a predict-the-mean baseline grew from 1 of 4 to 9 of 13 as the database expanded from 10 to 22 materials. While not a controlled comparison, this trend supports the premise that a precision-oriented, physics-checked database can power forward models beyond its training set and clarifies requirements for inverse material design.

title: Single-Cycle Battery Remaining Useful Life Prediction with Compressed Continuous Wavelet Features and Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are widely used in industrial applications, but their performance gradually degrades over time, making accurate lifetime prediction important for safety and reliability. However, reliable lifetime assessment generally requires extensive degradation testing, which is both costly and time-consuming. To reduce this burden, recent data-driven approaches have sought to predict the end-of-life cycle of batteries from only the initial few cycles. Nevertheless, identifying reliable degradation patterns from such limited early-cycle data remains challenging because early aging dynamics are often subtle and nonlinear. To address this issue, we adopt the continuous wavelet transform to convert cycle-wise voltage, current, and capacity signals into time-frequency representations, enabling multi-resolution characterization of degradation behavior. Building on this representation, we apply scale compression to reduce redundancy while preserving structural information in the scalograms. We evaluate the proposed framework on eight benchmark datasets derived from seven public battery datasets covering diverse electrode chemistries, cell form factors, and cycling protocols. Experimental results show that the proposed framework consistently outperforms prior approaches in single-cycle remaining useful life prediction and remains robust as the number of input cycles increases from 1 to 100. In addition, redundancy-fidelity analysis characterizes the trade-off introduced by scale compression, and gradient-based visual explanations indicate that the model focuses on localized time-frequency regions associated with structured signal transitions during charge-discharge operation. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and interpretability of the proposed framework for early-cycle battery remaining useful life prediction.

title: Elevated GANAB fuels PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint-mediated immune escape by maintaining PD-L1 stability in bladder cancer
abstract: BackgroundBladder cancer (BCa) is one of the most common malignancies of the urinary system, with limited treatment options and extremely poor prognosis in advanced stages. Although immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis have been approved for clinical use, the objective response rate remains low (15%-25%), and acquired resistance frequently develops. The molecular mechanisms underlying PD-L1-mediated immune evasion in bladder cancer remain incompletely understood.

title: Human CYP1A2 metabolism of organophosphorus pesticides and nerve agent surrogates
abstract: CYP1A2 contributes 13-15% of hepatic CYP450 content and plays a critical role in the metabolism of approximately 10% of pharmaceutical drugs in the human body. CYP1A2 has been previously reported to bioactivate and detoxify both the thion (P=S) and oxon (P=O) forms of organophosphorus (OP) compounds. In this study, we determined the capacity of CYP1A2 to degrade OP compounds using LC-MS/MS, as well as the inhibition of its activity by OP compounds using the previously developed pFluor50 assay.

title: Replacing H2O with D2O in cryo-EM reduces radiation damage in biological samples
abstract: Radiation damage limits the resolution achievable in electron microscopy of biological specimens. Hydrogen is the most abundant atom in these specimens, and its low mass maximizes the recoil energy it receives from incident electrons, making it the atom most readily lost under the beam. Substitution of hydrogen by deuterium halves this recoil energy and makes the bonds involved slightly harder to break, yet its protective effect on vitrified protein crystals has not been tested. Using cryogenic electron diffraction at 200 kV, we show that hen egg-white lysozyme crystals grown directly in D2O withstand a dose 1.7 times higher than crystals grown in H2O before their Bragg intensity at 10-7[A] falls to 1/e (13.2 {+/-} 1.0 against 7.7 {+/-} 0.4 e-/[A]2), with every D2O-grown crystal outlasting every H2O-grown crystal. The protection is achieved with deuteration confined mainly to the solvent and the exchangeable hydrogens at the protein surface, which form the hydrogen bonds that hold the crystal lattice together. The protein itself need not be deuterated by expression in deuterated media. Direct crystallization in D2O involves only a single substitution in the mother liquor and offers an accessible strategy to extend the usable dose in electron diffraction of protein crystals.

title: Removal of Lead and Arsenic from Contaminated Water Using a Sugarcane Bagasse Biochar–Metal Organic Framework (BC-MOF) Adsorbent
abstract: The presence of highly toxic metals in aquatic environments is a major environmental concern, affecting both ecosystems and human health. Conventional removal methods are often limited by high costs, low efficiency, and the generation of secondary waste. Biochar produced by the pyrolysis of sugarcane bagasse under oxygen-limited conditions is a sustainable alternative owing to its porous structure, which can retain metal contaminants.

title: Mass-Minimized Lunar Radiation Protection Using In Situ Regolith and Distributed Magnetic Shielding: Physics, Engineering Feasibility, and a Specification for Dose Validation
abstract: We evaluate a distributed superconducting perimeter fence for lunar surface protection against solar energetic particle (SEP) events. A relativistic Boris-pusher simulation shows that a 22-coil, two-channel fence attenuates SEP protons as effectively as a monolithic dipole of equal magnetic moment (94.9% versus 95.1% proton number-fluence removal; 75.4% versus 72.2% energy-fluence removal for a representative soft SEP spectrum), while leaving the protected volume field-free and avoiding a single point of failure. We then address two questions that determine buildability.

title: Roles of oxygen vacancies and the Ni–support interface in CO2 hydrogenation over Ni/Y-doped BaZrO3 revealed by experimental and computational studies
abstract: Understanding the roles of oxygen vacancies, proton-conducting supports, and metal–support interfaces is essential for the rational design of efficient CO2 hydrogenation catalysts. Herein, we investigate CO2 hydrogenation over Ni-supported Ydoped BaZrO3 (Ni/BZY) by combining powder X-ray diffraction (XRD), surface area measurements, CO2 temperatureprogrammed desorption (CO2-TPD), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), catalytic measurements, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.

title: Hunting the Enhanced Interaction of Donors with Post-Transition and Transition Metal Dichalcogenides: Comparative Study of NO 2 , H 2 S, NH 3 , and Aniline Adsorption on MoS 2 , SnS 2 , and ZrS 2 Monolayers
abstract: Two-dimensional transition and post-transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs and PTMDs) are promising materials for applications in roomtemperature, physisorption-based gas sensing and monitoring. In recent years, the mechanisms behind the adsorption of electron-accepting molecules have been well established, leading to the development of composition-engineering pathways that may be used to enhance the chemiresistive signal, as well as to design and fine-tune selective devices. However, similar trends have yet to be found for the electron-donating species.

title: Predicted structural models for NaSbBr4 and LiSbBr4 from a prototype-transplant search with machine-learned potentials and DFT
abstract: Many ternary halides studied for solid-state batteries have no reported crystal structure. Their computed stability then depends on whichever structure is assumed, so the 3D crystal structure is the bottleneck. We transplanted 228 prototypes from the Alexandria database into AMX4 chemistries (A = Li, Na; M = Al, Ga, In, Sc, Y, Sb, Bi; X = Cl, Br, I; 9431 transplants) and screened them with the MACE-MPA-0 machine-learned potential. We then compared the best survivors with every database-listed polymorph and competing phase we computed, using PBE-D3.

title: Constructive chemical discovery through autonomous reasoning and experiment
abstract: Making a new reaction often requires chemical knowledge that does not yet exist. Self-driving laboratories and language-model agents now plan, run and optimize experiments rapidly1–3, but deciding what to ask next still requires a chemist in the loop4. Here we report AIChemist, a robotic chemist for what we call constructive chemical discovery. It decides what to ask next from its own results, settles each question by calculation or experiment, and builds the next design on the answer.

title: Participant-level Raman spectroscopy of circulating EV-enriched fractions reveals distributed spectral differences in ischemic stroke patients
abstract: Raman spectroscopy provides a label-free vibrational profile of extracellularvesicle (EV)-enriched biofluid fractions. Participant-level Raman profiles were obtained from 97 participants with ischemic stroke and 50 controls. After quality control and region-specific normalization, spectra acquired at individual spatial sampling locations were aggregated into a single median spectrum per participant in the fingerprint (734–1788 cm −1 ) and C–H stretching (2451–3197 cm −1 ) regions, so that inference was carried out at the participant rather than the measurement level.

title: Role of water in hydrogen-based iron oxide reduction: effects on pore evolution and gas transport
abstract: Hydrogen-based direct reduction offers a low-emission route to ironmaking. Oxygen removal reduces the mass and volume of the solid, creating pores that provide pathways for hydrogen supply and removal of the water produced. Water accumulation within these evolving pores can inhibit further reduction. Here, we develop a phase-field model coupling water generation, transport, and reaction inhibition to pore evolution during wüstite-to-ferrite reduction. The simulations show that water accumulation slows reduction and allows pores to coarsen.

title: Co-Titration of Phosphatidylserine Lipids and a Channel Protein Using Constant pH Molecular Dynamics
abstract: The protonation state of anionic lipids plays a central role in regulating membrane electrostatics, structure, and interactions with membrane proteins. Lipid titration in membranes is inherently collective and strongly influenced by local composition and lateral organization. Experimentally, determining lipid p K ₐ values in heterogeneous and dynamically organized membranes is challenging, making it difficult to disentangle intrinsic lipid properties from collective membrane effects.

title: Capturing Transient Growth Windows for Narrow-Emitting Perovskite Nanoplatelets
abstract: Colloidal perovskite nanoplatelets offer thickness-tunable, directional emission, but maintaining narrow ensemble photoluminescence linewidths at greater thicknesses remains challenging. Here, we show that under selected reaction conditions, distinct CsPbBr3 nanoplatelet thickness populations emerge in succession during synthesis, each offering a transient window for isolation before further morphological evolution. By tuning growth kinetics through precursor composition and overall dilution under ambient conditions, we make these windows experimentally accessible.

title: Resistance without a detectable bindingenergy penalty: distinct dynamic defects of gatekeeper and molecular-brake mutations in FGFR1–erdafitinib recognition
abstract: The backbone Cα–Cα distance widely used to report kinase molecular-brake status gives a false negative under a clinically relevant FGFR1 resistance mutation: the brake's side-chain contact is destabilized in every replicate, yet the criterion reports it intact. Acquired FGFR1 kinase-domain mutations limit the clinical durability of erdafitinib, the first approved pan-FGFR inhibitor; loss of binding affinity is the assumed mechanism.

title: Dynamic Disproportionation Shapes Ga Sites in Silica-Supported Propane Dehydrogenation Catalysts
abstract: Ga is a key component of commercial propane dehydrogenation (PDH) catalysts. The regeneration of those catalysts involves oxidation and reduction cycles, the latter typically under H2 at about 550–650 °C. However, the structural evolution of Ga3+ sites under those strongly reducing conditions is underexplored. Here, we monitored the transformations of Ga3+ sites dispersed on a SiO2 support under H2 at 650 °C. The results show that this treatment generates metastable ºSiOGa1+ sites that disproportionate to Ga0 and Ga3+ sites.

title: Peptide nitrile ligation enables thioester-free chemical protein synthesis
abstract: Native chemical ligation has transformed chemical protein synthesis, yet its reliance on C-terminal peptide thioesters suffers from precursor preparation, stability and multisegment assembly. Here we report peptide nitrile ligation (PNL), a thioester-free ligation in which a stable C-terminal peptide nitrile is chemoselectively captured by an N-terminal cysteine and converted through a thiazoline intermediate into a native Xaa-Cys amide bond.

title: Assessing the Impact of Incorporating Bias-Adjusted
abstract: Understanding global ground-level ozone is hindered by significant monitoring gaps. To address this, we introduce a Bayesian Maximum Entropy data fusion framework that includes satellite ozone observations, generating a global 0.1° surface ozone dataset (2005–2022). Satellite observations (IASI+GOME2, OMI/MLS), adjusted to ground-level estimates, were analyzed using Flexible Regionalized Air Quality Model Performance to correct biases and estimate variance.

title: Consistency Testing of an Integrated SWRO–Brine Valorization Architecture: Alkalinity as the Binding Constraint
abstract: Integrated seawater reverse osmosis (SWRO) with brine valorization is widely proposed as a route to lower energy and near-zero liquid discharge, but such architectures are rarely tested against the physical bounds their stages must obey. Here a consistency-testing framework is applied to an architecture combining subsurface intake, isobaric energy recovery, membrane brine concentration, selective Ca/Mg precipitation and mechanical-vapor-compression crystallization. Each subsystem is checked against a thermodynamic or stoichiometric constraint rather than an assumed value.

title: How thermostats change the thermodynamic, structural and dynamic properties of a Lennard-Jones liquid
abstract: Almost every molecular dynamics simulation is coupled to a thermostat, and every thermostat modifies the equations of motion whose solutions are then interpreted as the physics of the system. The algorithms are well established and their qualitative artefacts are well known, yet a quantitative comparison of the commonly used schemes under one protocol, with the statistical resolution needed to detect their effects, is rarely reported, presumably because such effects are small compared with the run-to-run scatter of a typical simulation.

title: Disrupting Surface Oxo Availability Suppresses Ru Dissolution in RuO 2 Electrocatalysts
abstract: Ru loss from RuO 2 in acidic oxygen evolution requires availability of surface oxo (*O) for eruption of surface Ru to form adsorbed *RuO 4 . Screening 20 dopants on *O-covered RuO 2 (110) (DFT) gave a trend linking *RuO 4 formation to dopant-dependent *O activity. Durability testing (CP, ICP-MS) followed this trend for Mo- and Ta-RuO 2 . Zn- and Hf-RuO 2 retained more Ru than predicted; in situ near-ambient pressure XPS and online ICP-MS reveal that the two do so by different means. Zn inhibits Ru overoxidation while Hf welcomes it, yet both inhibit Ru eruption.

title: Behaviour of TMT labelled peptides in solid phase extraction, liquid chromatography, electrospray ionisation, and data-dependent acquisition
abstract: In bottom-up proteomics, quantification with isobaric labelling involves derivatising peptides with reagents that are isobaric when intact but upon fragmentation produce reporter ions of different masses. Peptides from different samples are labelled with different reagent isotopomers, and the reporter ion intensities serve as a readout for peptide abundance in different samples, enabling sample multiplexing. Increased chromatographic retention of labelled peptides has been described and considered in models predicting peptide retention.

title: Untargeted Lipidomics Reveals Dynamic Changes to the HEK 293T Lipidome During Lentiviral Vector Production Over 72 Hours
abstract: Lentiviral vectors (LV) are biotechnology tools descending from human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) that may be used in cell and gene therapies. HIV transduction efficiency has been shown to be negatively affected when the lipid composition of its envelope is altered, suggesting that targeted lipid envelope composition engineering may serve as a tool to modulate transduction. To investigate this possibility, an untargeted lipidomics experiment was conducted on HEK 293T packaging cells producing LV at three time points: 24, 48 and 72 h.

title: Sustainable Surface Metallurgy for Public Health: A Review of Barrier Degradation, Structural Heterogeneity, and Aluminum Leaching Dynamics in Low-Income Country Cookware
abstract: Aluminum (Al) consumer cookware remains a cornerstone of global food preparation due to its exceptional thermal efficiency and low cost. However, in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), the widespread reliance on low-purity, informally recycled artisanal alloys creates severe public health risks due to heavy metal migration into dietary pathways. This review explicitly links materials engineering for sustainable development with global safety frameworks by evaluating surface modification technologies designed to mitigate aluminum ion leaching under aggressive thermal and chemical cooking…

title: Footprint-aware Microkinetics Reveal Spatial Correlations with Catalytic Consequences
abstract: Metal catalysis often involves bulky molecules that cover catalyst surface areas beyond a single exposed metal atom. Common multi-site models account for adsorbate size with simple mean-field correction factors, but neglect how multi-site adsorbates become spatially correlated to avoid overlapping. Here, we combine prior theoretical constructions—the reduction of the Master equation in the fast-diffusion limit and the Widom insertion approach—to develop a footprint-aware microkinetic framework where adsorbates interact through hard exclusion.

title: Rapid One-Step Synthesis of Sodium-Ion Battery Cathodes from Desalination Waste: A Sustainable Approach to High-Performance Energy Storage
abstract: Desalination brine, a hypersaline byproduct of water treatment processes, represents an underutilized sodium feedstock with significant potential for battery material production. In this work, we report a streamlined rapid one-step synthesis (ROSS) method for Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 (NVP), a highperformance sodium-ion battery cathode material with demonstrated electrochemical comparability with lithium-based alternatives, directly from desalination brine.

title: An Enzyme-DNA Nanostructure with Enhanced Catalysis Accelerates MRSA Wound Healing
abstract: Antibiotic-resistant wound infections are a growing clinical challenge, as bacteria evade singletarget antimicrobials and persist within protective biofilms. Antimicrobial enzymes offer a promising alternative through their catalytic generation of bactericidal species, but their therapeutic utility is limited by instability in protease-rich wound environments. Here, we demonstrate that densely grafting short DNA strands onto lactoperoxidase (LPO), an innate immune enzyme, creates an enzyme-DNA nanostructure (Nano-Lac) with enhanced proteolytic stability and catalytic activity.

title: Anisotropic Electrical Conductivity in Close-Packed Two-Dimensional Polyaramids
abstract: Polyaramids such as Kevlar ® are renowned for their high mechanical strength and chemical resistance; however, their non-conjugated backbones render them electrically insulating. Orbital alignment can allow close-packed stacked molecules to exhibit long range conduction, opening the possibility that insulating nanomaterials may form conducting arrangements. Herein, we report two-dimensional (2D) polyaramids with tailored end-groups that promote tighter molecular packing as their size decreases.

title: Elucidating thermodynamic infeasibility of the (de)-lithiation process in 5V-class LiNi0.5Ge1.5O4 solid electrolyte
abstract: LiNi0.5Ge1.5O4 (LNGO), a Ge-substituted analogue of high-voltage cobalt-free LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 (LNMO) spinel cathode, has previously been reported to show electrochemical inertness up to 5V vs. Li+/Li. However, thermodynamic and electronic origins of this inert behaviour have remained unexplored. Herein, we investigated the redox mechanism and thermodynamic driving force governing the (de)intercalation behaviour of LNGO using first-principles density functional theory (DFT+U) and verified using experimental findings.

title: Revisiting Percolation and Molecular Diffusion in Disordered Pore Networks
abstract: The relationship between pore network structure and molecular diffusion in disordered nanoporous materials remains unclear. Here, we revisit two methodological choices that may contribute to inconsistent structure–diffusion relationships in the literature: percolation characterization and inclusion of non-percolating pores in diffusivity calculations. Our rigorous benchmarks show consistent results from Zeo++ and Mofography but reveal biased characterization from PoreBlazer due to limitations in its algorithm.

title: Semisyntheses of Aspercyclicins A and B via Isobenzofuran Cycloaddition
abstract: The recently isolated aspercyclicins A and B from Aspergillus sp. LI2020F001 represent a chimeric scaffold derived from crosstalk of two biosynthetic pathways. These natural products display cytotoxicity against cancer cell lines and potently activate immunogenic cell death (ICD). Herein, we report methodology development for biomimetic [4+2] cycloadditions involving an in situ generated isobenzofuran (IBF) leading to the semisyntheses of aspercyclicins A and B from the fungal-derived natural product (+)-geodin.

title: Methodological Optimization of ATR-IR Spectroelectrochemistry for Powdered and Poorly Conductive Electrocatalysts
abstract: In-situ infrared spectroscopy combined with electrochemistry has become a key tool for studying the processes that govern the activity of electrocatalysts under operating conditions. However, its application has been limited almost exclusively to model electrodes, which are either electronically conductive or specifically designed to maximise the ATR optical signal, thereby limiting its use for a family of emerging heterogenous catalysts typically available in powder form and exhibiting poor electrical conductivity.

title: Educational Interventions for Perinatal Depression Management Among Non-Specialist Providers in Resource-Constrained Settings: A Descriptive Systematic Review of Limited Evidence
abstract: This descriptive systematic review synthesizes evidence from resource-constrained primary and non-specialist care settings on the structural components of educational interventions for frontline health care workers regarding perinatal depression (PND). A comprehensive search was conducted across CINAHL, Cochrane Library, PubMed, and Scopus for experimental and quasi-experimental studies published between January 1, 2019, and August 31, 2025, in Resource-Constrained Settings.

title: Remote sensing applications in solid waste monitoring and management
abstract: The rapid growth of solid waste generation carries significant environmental and public health challenges globally. Traditional waste monitoring methods are not cost-effective and are limited in spatial and temporal scope. Remote sensing, encompassing satellite, aerial, and unmanned platforms, has emerged as a transformative approach to identify, monitor, and manage solid waste sites. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the state-of-the-art in remote sensing applications for solid waste monitoring and management, covering technological developments in the past 2 decades.
venue: Waste management & research : the journal of the International Solid Wastes and Public Cleansing Association, ISWA

title: Platelet-derived biomarkers in solid malignancies: a systematic review and meta-analysis of prognostic outcomes and diagnostic evidence
abstract: Platelets contribute to tumor angiogenesis, immune evasion, and metastasis, and baseline platelet indices have been proposed as accessible prognostic biomarkers for solid malignancies. Their clinical utility remains uncertain because prior studies have reported inconsistent comparison directions and cancer type-dependent effects. This PRISMA 2020-compliant, PROSPERO-registered (CRD420261350460) systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated platelet count (PLT), mean platelet volume (MPV), platelet distribution width (PDW), and plateletcrit (PCT) in patients with solid malignancies.

title: Generalization in Learning: Eyring Formula and Predator-prey Model
abstract: In this work, generalization in machine learning is investigated using a predator-prey model. We overview biological and chemical interpretation of the stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics and generative adversarial network. For a particular example of recovering an unknown function by a polynomial of fixed degree from a set of noisy data, the predator-prey model provides better approximation compared to the gradient descent method. Further, thermodynamical arguments, in particular Eyring formula, are used to explain grokking (delayed generalization) phenomenon in machine learning.

title: Depth-Aware Machine Learning for 3D Reconstruction of Fibrous Porous Electrodes by FIB-SEM Tomography
abstract: Quantitative three-dimensional reconstruction of porous polymers with sub-micrometer feature sizes is central to understanding and designing electrochemical interfaces and membranes. However, focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy tomography combined with conventional segmentation techniques cannot readily reconstruct complex disordered morphologies such as fibers. Standard segmentation workflows misclassify out-of-plane material as in-plane material, distorting the reconstructed pore network, fiber connectivity, and interface area. Here, we introduce an annotation-free, depth-aware machine-learning framework that combines monocular depth estimation, trained on macroscale images, with unsupervised clustering to separate in-plane polymer cross-sections from subsurface contributions in serial FIB-SEM tomography images. Applied to copper-coated electrospun poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) fiber mats, the approach produces 3D reconstructions that preserve fibrous morphology more faithfully than conventional supervised and unsupervised segmentation. Quantitative validation against capillary flow porometry, pycnometry, and high-resolution wide-angle X-ray computed tomography demonstrates improved agreement across pore cross-section diameter, fiber volume ratio, and Cu depth decrease metrics. This work establishes depth-aware segmentation as a transferable strategy from real-scale to nanoscale imaging, requiring no labeled training data and enabling accurate 3D segmentation and reconstruction from SEM images. This approach opens a path toward more reliable structure-property relationships in disordered porous polymer materials.

title: Peripheral immune tolerance as a driver of tumor immune escape and therapy resistance
abstract: Peripheral immune tolerance, essential for preventing autoimmunity, is increasingly co-opted by tumors to drive progression, metastatic dissemination, and immunotherapy resistance. Whereas central tolerance eliminates autoreactive clones, peripheral tolerance remains dynamically regulated by antigen persistence, cytokine gradients, metabolic cues, and stromal architecture, a plasticity that tumors exploit to build a multilayered immunosuppressive ecosystem.
venue: Clinical & translational oncology : official publication of the Federation of Spanish Oncology Societies and of the National Cancer Institute of Mexico

title: In-Solution Measurements of Binding Kinetics and Thermodynamics by nano Temperature Alteration Kinetics
