abstract: Binding kinetics are central to mechanism-driven drug discovery. Previously, we established Spectral Shift technology for the measurement of equilibrium binding affinity by detecting small shifts in the emission spectrum of a fluorescently labeled molecule upon binding to a ligand. While slow binding kinetics can be observed as a gradual change toward equilibrium after mixing the binding partners, faster interactions often have already reached equilibrium once the measurement is started. Here, we extend Spectral Shift to the measurement of fast binding kinetics through a method termed "nano Temperature Alteration Kinetics" (nanoTAK). A rapid temperature step perturbs the binding equilibrium of an enthalpically driven interaction, and the subsequent relaxation toward the new equilibrium is monitored in real time by recording the time-dependent Spectral Shift signal. The relaxation directly encodes the association rate kon and dissociation rate koff of the interacting molecules, which are extracted by fitting data of a full ligand dilution series to a global kinetic model. In addition, the fit also returns thermodynamic parameters of the interaction such as the binding enthalpy and entropy. We validate the approach across three tiers of molecular interactions. First, hybridization of a 10-mer DNA duplex serves as a model system with large binding enthalpy. Global fits match the data over three different temperature steps and confirm the accuracy of the derived fit model. Second, the kinase p38 with a set of six ATP-competitive and allosteric inhibitors demonstrates that the method extends to a classical protein-small molecule system with substantially smaller enthalpic changes, yielding consistent rate constants across compounds and temperatures and offering unique insights into their temperature dependence. Third, the degrader system consisting of VHL E3-ligase complex (VCB), PROTAC MZ1 and bromodomain 2 of BRD4 (BRD4(BD2)) illustrates the application to a higher-order system, revealing differences in the binding kinetics between the binary and ternary complex. The presented method can resolve interactions that re-equilibrate faster than within ~1 second, a timescale that can be difficult to access reliably with surface-based instruments. Binding kinetics can be measured both near room temperature, using a temperature step from 20 to 25 {degrees}C, but also, as an inherent feature of the approach, at physiologically relevant temperatures such as 37 {degrees}C.

title: USP4-Mediated Deubiquitination of PTBP1 Promotes Glioma Progression and Radioresistance by Enhancing PHB2-Dependent Mitophagy
abstract: Mitophagy plays a key role in glioma radioresistance, but its upstream regulatory mechanism is not fully understood. This study aims to investigate the function and potential molecular mechanism of polypyrimidine tract-binding protein 1 (PTBP1) in mitophagy and radioresistance of glioma. The GSE16011 dataset was used to screen the differentially expressed genes, combined with weighted gene co-expression network analysis and machine learning to screen the key genes related to mitophagy in glioma.

title: Hsp10 Targets the C-Terminus of α-Synuclein to Inhibit Secondary Nucleation and Remodel Labile Fibrils
abstract: Aggregation of a-synuclein is a central pathological feature of Parkinsons disease and related synucleinopathies. The co-chaperonin Hsp10, a component of the Hsp60/Hsp10 chaperonin system, has recently been proposed to possess independent chaperone activity and has been found to co-localize with a-synuclein aggregates in diseased brains, suggesting a role in regulating a-synuclein assembly. Here, we combine solution NMR spectroscopy, cryo-electron microscopy, and kinetic analyses to define a multistage mechanism by which Hsp10 modulates a-synuclein aggregation. Hsp10 transiently interacts with monomeric a-synuclein, with residues on the inner surface and top-loop regions of Hsp10 primarily engaging the acidic C-terminal region of a-synuclein. Hsp10 exerts a concentration-dependent, biphasic effect on aggregation, accelerating fibrillization at substoichiometric concentrations while inhibiting de novo aggregation at higher concentrations through suppression of secondary nucleation. Furthermore, Hsp10 decorates fibril surfaces through interactions with the exposed a-synuclein C-terminus, thereby limiting secondary nucleation. Hsp10 also promotes the disaggregation of thermodynamically labile fibrillar fragments. Together, these findings establish a mechanistic framework for Hsp10-mediated regulation of a-synuclein assembly and expand the functional landscape of Hsp10 beyond its canonical role in mitochondrial protein folding.

title: Data-Driven Investigation of Asymmetric Photo-Organocatalyzed Alkylation of Indoles
abstract: Enantioselective dual catalysis represents a powerful strategy for the preparation of functionally dense optically active compounds. Photocatalysis, paired with organocatalysis, undeniably represents a popular choice that takes advantage of radical and polar reactivity for crafting challenging bonds. Despite the interest in this methodology, the detailed analysis of the effects governing selectivity between the two catalytic cycles has not been extensively studied. Herein, we report a data-driven mechanistic study campaign to disclose the factors that influence the enantioselectivity of a photo-organocatalytic alkylation of indoles. Data science tools were used to generate a virtual library of potential substrates, thus ensuring the selection of a statistically diverse training set. Subsequent multivariate linear regression (MLR) analysis led to the identification of substrate electronic features as the key factor affecting the stereochemical outcome. Moreover, comprehensive mechanistic experiments unveiled the key role of the in situ generated oxindole intermediate that connects the two catalytic cycles in determining the observed selectivity. These findings lay the foundation for developing asymmetric dual catalytic transformations of synthetic relevance and provide a general platform for interrogating other complex catalytic systems.

title: Volatilomics in psychiatric biomarker research: from odor signatures to multiomic integration
abstract: Schizophrenia remains a major challenge in psychiatry, with diagnosis still relying largely on symptom-based assessments and lacking validated biomarkers for early detection, screening, or longitudinal monitoring. Although genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic studies have revealed systemic biological dysregulation involving immune, metabolic, and neurodevelopmental pathways, conventional multiomic approaches face significant translational limitations. They often require blood or tissue sampling and can be costly; although they include both dynamic, state-sensitive and more stable, trait-like signals, their complexity and sampling burden can limit frequent or population-level use. Volatilomics, the study of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emitted through breath, sweat, and skin, has emerged as a complementary molecular approach that may help address these gaps. VOCs represent dynamic downstream metabolic outputs and may capture rapid, state-dependent biochemical changes. Analytical and machine-learning studies have reported VOC pattern alterations in schizophrenia with promising classification accuracy in small, early-stage discovery cohorts, although independent external validation remains limited. This review examines volatilomics as a promising complementary approach with potential applications in early detection and longitudinal monitoring, and considers how integration with systemic multiomics could contribute to diagnosis, patient stratification, and precision psychiatry.
venue: European archives of psychiatry and clinical neuroscience

title: Decoding the Physical Mechanisms of Protein-Small Molecule Association by Multiscale Kinetic Monte-Carlo Simulations
abstract: Protein-small molecule association involves multiple recognition stages governed by distinct physical interactions, yet resolving their kinetic contributions remains computationally challenging. Here, we develop a multiscale Monte Carlo framework that combines an atomistic, conformationally flexible ligand with a coarse-grained protein binding pocket and an atomistic steric envelope. Association is decomposed into three stages: molecular encounter, pocket entry, and productive binding. We evaluate the framework using ten protein-ligand complexes representing nine distinct targets, with experimentally derived association rates spanning nearly four orders of magnitude. Simulated pocket-entry rates exhibit the strongest correspondence with experimental kinetics (Pearson r = 0.617; Spearman {rho} = 0.758), whereas productive-binding rates show closer agreement in absolute magnitude. Systematic perturbations of electrostatic interactions, hydrophobic attraction, hydrogen bonding, and ligand torsional flexibility reveal stage-dependent sensitivities. Initial encounter is comparatively insensitive to these perturbations, while hydrophobic attraction and conformational flexibility influence pocket entry. Productive binding exhibits additional sensitivity to local interactions, with excessive hydrogen-bond strengthening potentially hindering native-pose formation. Probability-derived kinetic-stage barriers and normalized mechanism descriptors further reveal heterogeneous recognition behavior across protein targets. Together, this framework provides a computationally efficient and interpretable approach for investigating protein-ligand association pathways and their physical determinants across diverse molecular systems.

title: Rapid femtosecond laser trenching accelerates cryo-electron tomography lamella workflows
abstract: Transmission electron microscopy requires electron-transparent specimens, typically below 200 nm thick. For cellular and tissue samples this is typically achieved by focused ion-beam (FIB) thinning to form lamellae. Milling times scale with specimen thickness, and high-pressure-frozen specimens more than 10 m thick can take up to 2 hours per lamella. We present a pre-processing approach in which bulk material is removed by ultrashort-pulse laser ablation prior to milling, rapidly generating large trenches in vitrified grids under cryogenic conditions and leaving material to be finished by conventional milling to yield electron-transparent lamellae. Laser ablation completes in seconds (4 seconds per pattern), compared with minutes to tens of minutes for FIB trench milling, and introduces negligible damage to the final lamellae. By replacing the most time-intensive, contamination-sensitive bulk-removal steps with seconds-long laser trenching, this open-source approach reduces time-to-lamellae, increasing throughput and preserves compatibility with standard cryo-FIB/SEM polishing and cryo-ET data-collection pipelines.

title: Dielectric Dynamics and Polar Nanoregions in Ferroelectric Nematic Liquid Crystals of the nJK Series
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive investigation of polarization dynamics and phase transitions in a novel homologous series of polar nematics (nJK, n=1-5) using broadband dielectric spectroscopy (DS). The analysis of dielectric spectra in planar and homeotropic cells revealed the evolution of relaxation mechanisms, transitioning from single-particle molecular reorientations in the isotropic phase to complex collective dynamics across the nematic (N), intermediate (N X ), and ferroelectric nematic (N F ) phases.

title: Computational Interactions between the Endohedral Metallofullerene Gd@C60 and Human Toll-Like Receptor 3: A Molecular Docking and Molecular Dynamics Study
abstract: Background: Endohedral metallofullerenes (EMFs), such as the gadolinium fullerene Gd@C60, are being explored as kinetically stable alternatives to gadolinium chelate contrast agents and as platforms for nanomedicine. Their behavior in a biological medium depends strongly on how they interact with proteins. Toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3) is an endosomal receptor that senses double-stranded RNA, and it is a relevant partner because nanoparticles are commonly internalized into endosomes. How Gd@C60 might bind to human TLR3 (hTLR3) is not known.

title: Field misalignment effect on the in-plane magnetoresistance in the high-temperature superconductor FeSe/SrTiO3
abstract: The azimuthal angular dependence of the in-plane magnetoresistance provides a powerful probe for detecting rotational symmetry breaking in superconductors, which has significant implications for understanding the superconducting pairing symmetry and the intertwined orders. However, in two-dimensional or layered superconductors with strong anisotropy between in-plane and out-of-plane critical fields, measuring the in-plane magnetoresistance is particularly challenging as it is extremely sensitive to the field misalignment. Here we perform systematic electrical transport measurements on ultrathin FeSe films grown on SrTiO3 substrates. By remounting the same FeSe film to change the field misalignment, two qualitatively different angular dependences of the in-plane magnetoresistance are observed in the superconducting transition region, indicating the extreme sensitivity of the measurement to field misalignment. The observed anisotropic in-plane magnetoresistance can be well captured by our geometric model considering the field misalignment effect. Our work provides a practical framework for disentangling the misalignment effect and investigating the in-plane rotational symmetry breaking in two-dimensional or layered superconductors.

title: Reasoning or Just Prompting? Probing the Mechanism of Latent Chemical Reasoning
abstract: Latent reasoning performs intermediate computation in continuous space rather than through explicit tokens, which is particularly appealing in chemistry, where errors in explicit reasoning can propagate to the final answer. Yet if latent states truly constitute an implicit reasoning chain, they should be causally important. We find otherwise: swapping or moderately perturbing intermediate latent states has little effect on performance, while removing them entirely sometimes causes a substantial score drop. Thus, the latent states matter, but their molecule-specific content appears to matter far less. This points to a simpler interpretation. Rather than encoding a step-by-step reasoning chain, latent states may primarily steer subsequent model computation, much like soft prompts. Indeed, a single fixed prefix shared across molecules reproduces LatentChem's performance, and a learned static soft prompt performs comparably to per-input latent generation in controlled models. The tolerance of latent sequences to substitution and moderate perturbation further supports this connection. We therefore suggest that latent chemical reasoning may be better viewed as soft prompting than as a reasoning chain hidden in continuous space.

title: Axion Quasibound States in the Continuum and Their Enhanced Axion Nonlinearity
abstract: Dynamical axion quasiparticles (DAQs) in condensed-matter systmes have emerged as a fascinating platform for exploring axion physics and nonlinear optical phenomena. However, the amplitude of the coherent oscillating $θ$ field is even smaller than that of the static counterpart, making the experimental observation of DAQs particularly challenging. Here, we introduce symmetry-sensitive bound states in the continuum (BICs) physics to enable the all-optical detection of DAQs and enhance DAQ-mediated second-harmonic generation (SHG). Specifically, we uncover that DAQs induce optical shear that breaks the $C_{2z}$ symmetry of metagratings without geometric engineering, thereby converting symmetry-protected BICs into axion quasi-BICs (qBICs). In this context, the evolution of the quality factor and topological charge in momentum space, together with the appearance of optical resonances in far field associated with axion qBICs, offers achiral optical signatures for DAQ detection beyond the widely used Kerr and Faraday effects. Furthermore, by exploiting axion qBICs in the critical coupling regime to enhance fundamental optical field, we show that the SHG efficiency can be enhanced more than $10^5$-fold compared to bulk axion materials, achieving a conversion efficiency exceeding $10^{-6}~W^{-1}$. The SHG is governed by the magnetoelectric coupling, which differs from that in conventional SHG materials. Our findings establish a new approach for probing DAQs via achiral optical effects, while providing a versatile route for reconfigurable photonics and terahertz nonlinear optics.

title: Primary Human Macrophages Exhibit Functional CYP3A4 Activity with Marked Expression-Function Discordance and Cocaine-Induced Catalytic Activation
abstract: CYP3A4 is a phase I drug-metabolizing enzyme responsible for transformation of ~50% of clinically relevant drugs. While extensively characterized in hepatocytes, its role in immune cells remains poorly understood. Here, using primary human monocyte-derived macrophages, we identify an understudied extrahepatic site of CYP3A4-mediated drug metabolism. Macrophages from 100 independent donors expressed CYP3A4 and its transcriptional regulators, Pregnane X Receptor (PXR) and Constitutive Androstane Receptor (CAR), with substantial interindividual variability. Importantly, CYP3A4 protein expression was accompanied by measurable catalytic activity in intact macrophages, yet CYP3A4 mRNA, protein abundance, and activity lacked concordance, demonstrating that expression alone may not predict function. In vivo, CYP3A4 was expressed in rhesus macaque Kupffer cells, further supporting macrophages as a potential pharmacologic entity. We next evaluated cocaine as a potential modulator of CYP3A4, due to its role in xenobiotic clearance. Cocaine had a dichotomous effect on expression, increasing CYP3A4 in some donors while producing no change or decreases in others, a phenotype associated with PXR, CAR, and the sigma-1 cocaine receptor. Strikingly, despite these divergent expression responses, cocaine increased CYP3A4 catalytic activity in all donors, reaching or exceeding levels induced by rifampicin, a clinically relevant CYP3A4 inducer. In rhesus macaques, cocaine also decreased antiretroviral therapy tissue concentrations, coincident with increased CYP3A4 and PXR. Together, these findings establish macrophages as a functionally active extrahepatic site of CYP3A4 metabolism and reveal a critical disconnect between CYP3A4 expression and catalytic function. Moreover, our findings identify interindividual variability and expression-activity discordance as important considerations for personalized medicine and understanding clinically relevant drug-drug interactions in the context of substance use.

title: Protein Folding Interference Enables Selective Cyclin D1 Degradation
abstract: Cyclin D1 is a central regulator of cell-cycle progression and a compelling therapeutic target in cancer, yet its non-enzymatic function, limited ligandability, and rapid turnover have hindered direct pharmacological intervention. Here we show that these limitations can be overcome by targeting a transient conformational state populated during protein folding.

title: Deep Scientific Reasoning under Physical Constraints: Structure-Aware Spectrum Prediction
abstract: Structured scientific spectra encode rich physical information while obeying hard constraints, such as conservation laws and characteristic spectral geometry. Accurate prediction of these spectra is central to materials discovery, yet existing methods often treat them as unconstrained sequences and therefore fail to enforce the underlying physical structure. Taking electronic density of states (eDOS) as the prototypical example, we introduce DeepSciReasoner, a general paradigm for predicting scientific spectra under physical constraints. The framework combines structure-aware spectrum decoding with constraint-preserving physical reasoning, allowing predictions to capture rich spectral structure while respecting the underlying physics. We evaluate DeepSciReasoner on eDOS, phonon density of states (phDOS), X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES), and Raman spectra, where it substantially improves prediction accuracy while maintaining physical consistency. These results establish DeepSciReasoner as a reusable blueprint for structured scientific spectrum prediction under hard physical constraints.

title: Designing sustainability under Earth-system rate constraints
abstract: Sustainability debates are monopolized by quantities: total energy use, material stocks, or recycling volumes. These metrics are informative, but they obscure a more fundamental constraint. On a materially closed but energetically open Earth, long-term viability is governed by rates: power density, areal power density, and the rate at which dispersed materials can be repurified under dif- fuse solar fluxes. We develop a physical framework that links technological metabolism, material dilution, and recycling limits through these rate con- straints. This perspective clarifies why many contemporary technologies remain viable only through stock drawdown and high-power buffering, and why green growth strategies often shift rather than resolve the underlying mismatch between industrial activity and Earth-system dynamics. We argue that long-term sustain- ability requires both quantitative reduction in aggregate industrial throughput toward rate-bounded regimes and the development of technologies qualitatively compatible with biospheric operating conditions.

title: TCSP3.0: Template-Based Crystal Structure Prediction with Coefficient-Preserving Element Substitution and Structural Diversity
abstract: Template-based crystal structure prediction (CSP) transfers a known crystal structure to a new composition by element substitution, so its accuracy depends on retrieving suitable templates, mapping elements and ranking the resulting candidates correctly. Auditing the original TCSP2.0 implementation on the T180 benchmark, we found that 469 of its 2,347 selected structures (20%) have the wrong composition, caused by element mappings that ignore stoichiometric coefficients and by sequential text substitution that cascades or corrupts element symbols. We propose TCSP3.0, which enforces coefficient-preserving mappings, substitutes species simultaneously on parsed structures and validates every candidate's composition and cell. It further adds periodic-number retrieval, soft oxidation-state evidence, radius-compatibility scoring, structural deduplication, and ORB-v3 machine-learning-potential relaxation and energy ranking of its candidates, as used by deep generative CSP baselines. TCSP3.0 achieves Top-1 and Top-20 match rates of 72.2% and 90.6% on T180, compared with 28.3% and 45.6% for TCSP2.0, and a Top-20 match rate of 74.0% on a new 800-target benchmark (T800). On T180 it also outperforms PNcsp+ and deep generative models CrystalFlow and MaskGXT (Top-1 72.2% versus at most 63.9%). Even without relaxation, TCSP3.0 reaches 67.8% at Top-1 and 90.6% at Top-20 in a median of 28 s per target on two CPU cores, about ten times faster than CrystalFlow. Paired ten-arm ablations on T180 and T800 show that most of the improvement comes from the correctness fixes; structural deduplication significantly improves the Top-5 match rate, embedding-based retrieval is required for coverage, and the remaining scoring features have small or null effects.

title: Bridging Spectroscopy and Reactivity: Identifying the True Reactive CO Species in Electrocatalytic CO Oxidation
abstract: In situ electrochemical vibrational spectroscopy has revolutionized our understanding of electrocatalysis. However, establishing a rigorous correlation between spectroscopic signatures and reaction kinetics is still very challenging because high-coverage surface species may dominate the signal, whereas the truly reactive participants may be short-lived or spectroscopically silent.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Momentum-selective graphene spectroscopy of moiré excitons
abstract: Far-field photoluminescence probes only the light-cone corner of an exciton's momentum content, whereas energy transfer to nearby graphene integrates in-plane momenta up to the inverse spacer thickness $1/z$. For a WSe$_2$/MoSe$_2$ heterobilayer we build the transition polarization $\bm{P}_n(\qv)$ of each localized moiré exciton from the registry-dependent vector dipole texture and use each $\bm{P}_n$ for both baths. The two baths rank the states differently: the graphene-rate ratios differ from the optical ones, their ordering inverts with spacer thickness, and the distance exponents at $z=10$\,nm spread by more than two units. These ratios are independent of the transition-dipole prefactor. Within the $C_3$-symmetric leading-harmonic model the chiral $p_+$ and $d_-$ states are also dark at normal incidence yet transfer to graphene at rates comparable to the bright ground state. Their graphene rate depends on the sign of the texture phase, a quantity invisible in far-field emission, which we determine from first principles. In a device this prediction requires a splitting, larger than the symmetry-breaking mixing, that protects the chiral partners. Graphene proximity thus acts as a momentum-selective near-field probe of moiré excitons, and we propose its use as a practical spectroscopy.

title: Synovial fluid glycosaminoglycans signature involved 3-O-sulfated heparan sulfate modulated by TGF-β pathway in OA
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) involved extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling of cartilage associated to inflammatory activation of fibroblastic like synoviocytes (FLS) from the synovium, but the molecular crosstalk between these two compartments remains poorly understood. Among Glycosaminoglycans (GAG) compound from ECM, heparan sulfate (HS) specifically regulate the bioavailability and activity of Heparin Binding Proteins (HBP), including cytokines and growth factors, such as TGF-{beta}, whose aberrant bioavailability in the synovial fluid (SF) could drive the catabolic process. Here, we investigated the composition, sulfation patterns and biological activities of GAG from OA SF that are currently uncharacterized and explored the regulation of 3-O-sulfated HS in TGF-{beta} mediated response in FLS. Total GAG from 52 OA-SF SF were extracted and quantitatively characterized by DMMB assay and HPLC. They are functional since they are able to bind several HBP with pleiotropic inflammatory and angiogenic properties according to ELISA competitive binding assay. They were able also to transactivate HBP signaling in cellular tests in-vitro, since they potentiated proliferative properties on fibroblastic and endothelial cells, and induced altered metabolic and inflammatory markers expressions in murine chondrocytes and human FLS. Although HS represented a minor fraction of SF-GAG, they contained a rare tri-sulfated disaccharidic fraction distinct from GAG from cartilage. Same GAG characterization was performed on FLS expanded from SF and SM samples. FLS exhibited also a rare sulfation pattern of 3-O-Sulfated HS on their surface analyzed by immunofluorescent staining, associated with the expression of 4 isoforms of 3-O-sulfotransferase (HS3ST) identified by RT-qPCR. TGF-{beta}1 treatment of FLS culture increases HS3ST expression profiles and HS sulfation pattern through the SMAD2/3 pathway, as observed by RT-qPCR, IF and western blot respectively. Finally, combined siRNA mediated silencing of these HS3ST enzymes affects FLS inflammatory secretome, according to proteome profiler cytokine arrays. among pro-inflammatory CXCL10 and CCL5 chemokines. Altogether, these data identify OA SF-GAG as new effective modulator of joint cell responses and reveal for the first time 3-O-sulfated HS and HS3ST patterns of expression in OA FLS associated with TGF-{beta}-Smad2/3-signaling pathway. Such specific HS fractions may contribute to the regulation of synovial inflammatory secretome, according to HBP partners that need to be further identified. However, this new glycanic mechanistic pathway sustaines the involvement of HS in OA progression and subsequently their interest as glycanic therapeutic targets.

title: Transition Metal-Anchored Newly Synthesized Aza-Triphenylene Monolayer for Efficient Hydrogen Evolution Reaction: Insights from DFT
abstract: First-principles calculations were employed to explore the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity in two-dimensional aza-triphenylene monolayers functionalized with transition metals. Among the various metals studied, Co, Ru, and Y demonstrate outstanding catalytic efficacy, lowering the hydrogen adsorption free energy from -0.78 eV for pure aza-triphenylene to 0.05, 0.20, and 0.06 eV, respectively. Volcano plot analysis corroborates their enhanced HER activity. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations confirm thermal stability, while the electronic structure and charge transfer analysis reveal the strong catalyst-surface interaction. Metal decoration also improves the carrier mobility, particularly for Ru-functionalized aza-triphenylene. The climbing-image nudged elastic band calculations for Co-functionalized aza-triphenylene exhibit activation barriers of 1.61, 2.29, and 5.88 eV for the Volmer, Heyrovsky, and Tafel reactions, respectively, highlighting a preferred Volmer-Heyrovsky route with the Heyrovsky being the rate-determining step. These findings highlight the potential of transition-metal-functionalized aza-triphenylene as a promising platform for developing efficient HER electrocatalysts.

title: Crystal-surface polarity enables nonreciprocal transport in a centrosymmetric kagome magnet
abstract: Every crystal surface breaks inversion symmetry even when the bulk is centrosymmetric, creating an intrinsic boundary polarity ($\mathbf{\mathit{P}}$). Here we show that this polarity enables zero-field nonreciprocal transport in the centrosymmetric kagome magnets TbMn$_6$Sn$_{6-x}$In$_x$. In symmetric TbMn$_6$Sn$_{4.4}$In$_{1.6}$ microdevices, opposing side surfaces exhibit second-harmonic longitudinal resistances of comparable magnitude and opposite sign. Reversing the spontaneous magnetization ($\mathbf{\mathit{M}}$) reverses both signals, whereas rotating $\mathbf{\mathit{M}}$ so that the toroidal moment $\mathbf{\mathit{P}} \times \mathbf{\mathit{M}}$ has no component along the current suppresses the response. In pristine TbMn$_6$Sn$_6$, the signal switches off across the spin-reorientation transition, providing a chemically ordered control of the same symmetry relation. Spatial potential mapping indicates that the nonlinear boundary contribution is distinct from the bulk linear conduction. Spin-orbit-coupled surface states associated with topological bands may enhance the effect. Crystal-surface polarity therefore offers a broadly applicable route to zero-field rectification in centrosymmetric magnetic conductors around room temperature.

title: Phase fluctuations dominated superconductivity in a thick Granular Boron-Doped Diamond film
abstract: We investigate the superconducting properties of a 1.2-μm-thick granular boron-doped diamond film, where tightly packed grains form a disordered network of Josephson junctions. The film exhibits a sharp superconducting transition at a critical temperature, T_c ~ 3 K. Its transport properties are well described by the Ambegaokar-Halperin theory of phase fluctuations. Direct measurements of the penetration depth using a two-coil mutual inductance technique reveal classic phase-fluctuation-dominated behavior: below T_c, the superfluid density (n_s) varies linearly over a wide temperature range - a hallmark of thermal phase fluctuations - before crossing over to a T^2 dependence at ultra-low temperatures. Both the large low-temperature penetration depth, λ(0) ~ 8.8 μm, and the slope of the linear ns variation in the thermal regime reveal a remarkably low superfluid stiffness in the range of 0.5-0.8 K. These results establish granular boron-doped diamond films as an excellent model system for investigating the role of long-wavelength phase fluctuations in three-dimensional superconductors.

title: Photoredox-Mediated Three-Component Carboamination of Reverse Exo -Glycals: Modular Access to C 4-Quaternary Furanosides and Spironucleosides
abstract: Quaternary stereocenters on densely functionalized furanoside frameworks are challenging to construct with high chemo-, regio-, and stereocontrol, especially in the presence of nitrogen-containing motifs and multiple downstream diversification handles. Here, we disclose a sequence-programmed three-component radical carboamination of reverse exo-glycals that provides modular access to C4-quaternary furanosides through a distinct radical retrosynthetic logic.
